title: Halloween Before Trick-or-Treat: What Indiana's Old Newspapers Reported

sources.what: Whiting, 1906: 'About ten extra policemen in addition to the usual force'; gates 'mysteriously carried away'; 'another window being broken, this time at Recht's Department store'
sources.who: Whiting-Robertsdale Historical Society, 'Halloween Has Always Brought Out the Wickedly in Whiting' (2018), quoting the paper

sources.what: Whiting, 1909: 'more quietly ... than it ever has been'; 'door mats and gates were stolen by the wholesale'; 'someone put soap on the rails'; the motorman had 'to get off the car and throw sand on the rails'
sources.who: Whiting-Robertsdale Historical Society (2018), quoting the paper
Lake County Times (Hammond), via Library of Congress, Chronicling America

sources.what: earliest known printing of 'tricks or treats': Sault Daily Star, Sault Ste. Marie, Ont., Nov. 1, 1917
Anoka, Minn., 1920: a citywide parade to keep pranksters busy
Anoka's 1920 parade and its anti-prank purpose

beats.text: Before trick-or-treat, Halloween in northwest Indiana was a night of pranks, and the papers kept score.
beats.label: NORTHWEST INDIANA

beats.text: In 1906, Whiting put about 10 extra policemen on watch. Gates still vanished, and a window was broken at Recht's department store.
beats.label: WHITING, INDIANA, 1906
beats.credit: As quoted by the Whiting-Robertsdale Historical Society

beats.text: In 1909, the paper said Halloween had gone more quietly than ever. Then it listed the damage.
beats.label: WHITING, INDIANA

card.label: HALLOWEEN
card.note: "MORE QUIETLY THAN IT EVER HAS BEEN"

beats.credit: As quoted by the Whiting-Robertsdale Historical Society

beats.text: Door mats and gates were stolen by the wholesale. Somebody soaped the streetcar rails, and the motorman had to climb down and throw sand on them.
beats.label: THE DAMAGE, 1909

card.by: THE PAPER, 1909, VIA WHITING-ROBERTSDALE HIST. SOCIETY

beats.credit: As quoted by the Whiting-Robertsdale Historical Society

beats.text: By the 1920s, some towns tried to tame the night with parties and parades. Anoka, Minnesota, started its Halloween parade in 1920.
beats.label: THE 1920s
beats.credit: Mental Floss; Star Tribune; Wisconsin Historical Society

beats.text: And trick-or-treat? Its earliest known printing, from 1917 in Ontario, meant just what it said: a treat, or a trick.
beats.label: THE WORDS

beats.text: What did Halloween look like where you grew up? Tell us in the comments.

factcheck.result: Lines 3, 4, 6, 7 supported. Changed: 'northwest Indiana' (line 1); 'It didn't help' dropped (line 2); Anoka named as the 1920s example (line 5); History.com credit dropped; the 1906 and 1909 reports credited as quoted by the Whiting-Robertsdale Historical Society because the Lake County Times scans in the repo are too low-resolution to read; no courthouse tower over Whiting.
